overview: Black develops the queen's knight first and keeps ...e5 or ...Nf6 for later. After 2.Nc3 Black plays ...e5 or ...Nf6, reaching a Reversed Sicilian or Anglo-Indian type of game. White usually keeps the extra tempo with Nc3, g3, Bg2 and d3 or d4. Games are positional and transpose often.

white_ideas.idea: Nc3, g3, Bg2 and d3, then e4 or a queenside space grab with a pawn advance.
Strike with d4 after Black commits to ...e5, to take the centre.

black_ideas.idea: Set up a Reversed Sicilian with ...e5, ...Nf6 and ...g6 and ...Bg7.
Transpose to a Four Knights or a King's Indian structure.

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Sicilian: White c4 and Nc3, Black pawn on e5 and d6, a fianchettoed bishop on g2.

character.notes: Quiet developing moves and slow manoeuvring; no early forcing lines.

soundness.notes: Playable for Black. White keeps a small edge at most.

structure.notes: Flank opening with the centre undecided; both sides can still choose their pawn set-up.

approach.notes: Black's 1...Nc6 is a rare reply to 1.c4, seldom played by strong players.

level.notes: Few theoretical lines, but needs sound positional judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2.d4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. c4 Nc6 2. d4 e5 3. d5 Nce7
sublines_that_differ.how: White gains space and Black has a awkward knight.

character.reason: Quiet flank play, neither forcing nor a fortress.

structure.reason: English-type flank opening with an undecided centre.

approach.reason: A rare reply for strong players.
